key_insight: Specialized, physics-driven machine learning force fields are needed to reliably model complex materials dynamics where general-purpose MLIPs fail under reactive, strained, open, or nonlocal conditions.
engineering_relevance: For atomistic simulation workflows, the review shows that choosing and validating an MLIP must be matched to the target observable, system physics, and computational budget rather than relying on broad zero-shot accuracy.
method: Survey trade-offs in MLIP design: representation limits, message-passing cost, and missing nonlocal physics.
Compare four demanding use cases: electrified interfaces, open systems, multiphase evolution, and fracture.
Use observable-specific benchmarking to judge whether a specialized or foundation-model approach is appropriate.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a systematic evaluation across four challenging application contexts and emphasizes benchmarking against intended observables rather than only near-equilibrium accuracy.
watch_item: High-order or heavily specialized models may improve physics fidelity but can become too costly or still miss out-of-distribution reactive states if not validated on the exact target phenomenon.
paper_title: Specialized machine learning force fields for materials dynamics
